problem_framing.rationale: Frames the decision exactly as posed (whether, and by which route) and compares A, B and J in one table against the board's own limits: $18M cap, payback by end-2030, 8% margin floor, with the $40M ambition shown separately. The one-launch bandwidth constraint is used to position Japan as the alternative and 2028 fallback. The issues the answer turns on (ad cost for payback, awareness for retail, the ambition shortfall) are named in the governing thought and executive summary. Nothing material is missing.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question and carries its main condition. The five summary points are the five sections, and every content slide title is a claim that the slide's numbers support. Titles alone give the argument: opportunity, why not retail, why Amazon, what it must survive, how to launch. Blemishes are minor: the same cash and revenue series recur on slides 10, 13, 14, 17 and 23, and slide 18's title overstates what labels and repeat have been shown to do for payback. Neither breaks the hierarchy.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I rebuilt the model and every figure checks: Amazon contribution $10.73 before ads, $4.73 / $4.01 / $3.05 at 25% / 28% / 32%; A cumulative cash +$2.40M / +$0.38M / -$2.32M / -$6.37M; break-even ACoS 28.6%; B peak -$20.8M and 4.5% group margin in 2027; the B-minus-A bridge of $23.2M; Japan +$1.8M. The duty case (-$0.63M, break-even 27.1%) differs from the key's -$0.74M only because it applies the rise from 2028, which is labelled. All four critical evidence items are used, including evidence against the recommendation (32% median, two stalled Amazon-first brands, repeat below benchmark). The correlation and the $5.2B figure are handled correctly. It falls short of 5 on three counts. The Japan comparison switches to operating profit before inventory and claims Japan earns more 'only' at 32%, when the document's own table shows Japan ahead on cumulative cash at 28% ($1.8M vs $0.4M) and the profit crossover is near 28.4%. Several mechanism claims are asserted without pack support (repeat orders carry little ad cost, fees cannot be negotiated). And there is no sensitivity on Option A volumes, although the document notes two of three Amazon-first entrants stayed below $5M.

strategic_judgment.rationale: The recommendation is clear, defensible and matches the key's preferred answer: Amazon-led with gates, retail only when awareness supports 4.0+ units, and $40M reset to after 2030. Moving the CEO's awareness trigger from 15% to 20% is argued from Table 8 (the 10–20% median of 3.5 is below the delisting line), and the door test replaces a national launch. Alternatives are compared on the board's criteria, and Japan is kept as a fallback. Weaknesses are material. The 28% gate leaves almost no headroom against a 28.6% break-even, and the document's own duty case puts break-even at 27.1%, so the gate could be passed and payback still missed. The gate is read at 12 months, before the $5M–$20M scale at which the benchmark says ad cost rises. Failing it leads to 'hold expansion', not a defined exit or a cost lever. The repeat gate has no threshold. Japan's better cumulative cash at pilot ad cost is underweighted, and volume risk is not gated.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer and its key condition are on the first content slide, the language is plain ('ad cost' for ACoS), and derivations are shown briefly. But the deck runs 25 slides for a decision that needs about 12: five section dividers, an appendix contents page, and repeated presentation of the same cash and revenue series. Length is somewhat out of proportion, though nothing is buried.

unsupported_claims.quote: Every repeat order is a sale with little or no ad cost
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives no data on ad cost by order type; the mechanism is asserted as fact. The same applies to 'TikTok discovery and repeat buyers bring sales Onsoo does not pay Amazon for'.

unsupported_claims.quote: Japan earns more only if US ad cost runs at the 32% agency median
unsupported_claims.why: Overstated. On the document's own operating-profit basis the crossover is about 28.4%, and on cumulative cash (its slide 13 table) Japan is already ahead at the pilot's 28%: $1.8M vs $0.4M.

unsupported_claims.quote: Amazon fees: referral and fulfillment take 36% of the price and cannot be negotiated
unsupported_claims.why: The 36% is correct, but the pack says nothing about whether the fees can be negotiated.

unsupported_claims.quote: Retail entry: A small door test, kept only at 4.0+ units a week (CEO: National launch)
unsupported_claims.why: The CEO's hypothesis says only 'add specialty beauty retail from 2029'. The national 600-door launch is the independent board member's proposal, not the CEO's.

unsupported_claims.quote: K-beauty is growing fast on Amazon
unsupported_claims.why: The pack shows K-beauty growth overall and Amazon's 2025 channel share. It gives no growth figure for K-beauty on Amazon.

unsupported_claims.quote: Three pilot gaps decide whether the Amazon route pays back: ad cost, repeat purchase and Korean-only labels
unsupported_claims.why: Only ad cost is shown to drive payback. No link from repeat rate or labels to cash is quantified or supported by the pack.

recommendation.summary: Approve an Amazon-led US launch in 2027. Gate ad cost at the pilot's 28% after 12 months, with Japan as the 2028 fallback if it fails. Enter specialty retail only through a small door test once aided awareness passes 20%, kept only at 4.0+ units per door per week. Put US-compliant labels on every unit from launch, and treat $40M as a goal for after 2030.
recommendation.rationale: Meets all four defensibility criteria. It compares A, B and J on cap, payback and margin floor. It tests the 25% ACoS and 4.5 units/door assumptions against the benchmarks. It states the payback condition (ACoS below about 28.6%, or 27.1% with the duty rise) and sets gates. It says explicitly that no route reaches $40M by 2030 within the limits. The weak point is that the 28% gate has almost no headroom and the consequence of failing it is loosely defined.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: Keeps the CEO's Amazon-first route, which the evidence supports, and modifies it where the evidence requires. It adds an ad-cost gate because payback fails above about 28.6% against a 32% scaling median. It raises the retail awareness trigger from 15% to 20% because the 10–20% band's median of 3.5 is below the 4.0 delisting line. It replaces a broad retail roll-out with a door test and resets $40M to after 2030. It surfaces the contradictions between the plan's 25% ACoS and the benchmark, the 4.5 units/door and Onsoo's awareness band, and the correlation memo and causation. The two unsupported causal claims are that repeat orders carry little ad cost, and that repeat and labels 'decide' payback.

output.overall_comment: Very strong document. The financial rebuild is exact on every figure I re-derived, including the Option B bridge, the ACoS sensitivities, the break-even and the group margins. It reaches all nine key insights, avoids all seven traps and lands on the key's preferred recommendation, with one refinement beyond the key: the 20% awareness trigger justified from the sell-through bands. Three things keep it from full marks. The Japan comparison is tilted by using operating profit before inventory, and it overstates the case ('only' at 32%) when the document's own table shows Japan ahead on cumulative cash at the pilot's ad cost. The 28% gate sits almost on the break-even, and under the document's own duty case it sits above it; the timing is early and the fail consequence is soft. And Option A's volumes are never stress-tested. A handful of mechanism claims are not supported by the pack, and the deck is roughly twice as long as the decision needs.
